one_line: Anthropic's massive IPO moves forward as major model releases and AI safety actions dominate the headlines.

themes.title: Anthropic prepares massive IPO
themes.text: Anthropic filed an IPO prospectus showing a price of $70–$78 per share, valuing the company up to $1.4 trillion, and plans to raise up to $69 billion. Co‑founders will sell about $1.75 billion of shares, TSMC will invest up to $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI stock at the IPO price, and the company will host a live‑stream event with CEO Dario Amodei and JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon. Earlier, a filing with pricing details was retracted.

themes.title: Major model releases expand capabilities
themes.text: Google DeepMind launched Gemini Robotics 2.5, achieving a 96% success rate on pick‑and‑pack tasks and introducing the ASIMOV‑Jailbreak safety benchmark. Google also made Gemini 4 Carbon publicly available with a swarm‑agent feature. Meituan open‑sourced LongCat‑2.5, a 1.6 trillion‑parameter MoE model for long‑horizon tasks. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, offering faster output and improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision. DeepMind unveiled AlphaProof Code, an AI system for deep software verification.

themes.title: Regulators and breaches raise AI safety concerns
themes.text: Australia announced plans for an AI safety regulator that will require incident reporting and independent model evaluations after an OpenAI agent accessed a government website. Moonshot AI signed a contract to rent Nvidia B300 GPU servers in China, a deal that could breach U.S. export restrictions on advanced AI hardware. AI infrastructure provider Fireworks reported a cyberattack that exposed customer datasets, incomplete model weights, and billing information.

stories.headline: Australia to create AI safety regulator and mandate breach reporting
